DUPLICATE NAME: col C also carries "Self-Efficacy" (observed in col-C.tsv) — assembler must keep one; this row is the generalized-belief (GSE) reading, C's is presumably the striving/mastery reading.

definition: Kindness, common-humanity and mindful balance toward oneself in failure or pain.

definition: Living in accord with one's own values and felt self rather than external pressure.
taxonomy: Wood Authenticity Scale (2008) · Kernis & Goldman multicomponent model

(2008) Psychol Sci 19(11):1140-1145 DOI:10.1111/j.1467-9280.2008.02215.x PMID:19076486 [VERIFIED-2] is the PubMed-indexed daily-diary evidence. Wood's scale has three subscales (self-alienation, authentic living, accepting external influence); the L-row scales the total.

definition: Degree to which one has settled on firm answers about who one is and what one stands for.
neighbors: Self-Concept Clarity · Moral Identity · Openness (other column)
taxonomy: Marcia identity status · Luyckx DIDS commitment dimensions

Commitment (DIDS commitment-making + identification) gives a rollable row whose L6 is Marcia's foreclosure — committed without exploring. Exploration is the JUDGED hidden axis: L1-L2 may be exploring or merely adrift.

definition: Cynical, strategic willingness to manipulate others for one's own ends.
taxonomy: Christie & Geis Mach-IV · Jones & Paulhus SD3 · Dahling MPS

flair_2: Robert Greene — The 48 Laws of Power (Viking, 1998) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_48_Laws_of_Power [VERIFIED-1]

Muris et al. warn the three dark traits overlap heavily (all load on low Honesty-Humility) — E2-1, E2-2, E2-4 will co-vary; the assembler may treat E2 as one cluster with four flavours. Greene is flair as a how-to text, not evidence.

definition: Inflated self-importance with exhibitionism, entitlement and a hunger for admiration.
taxonomy: Narcissistic Personality Inventory (Raskin & Terry) · SD3 Narcissism
formal_1: Raskin R & Terry H (1988). A principal-components analysis of the Narcissistic Personality Inventory and further evidence of its construct validity. J Pers Soc Psychol 54(5):890-902. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.54.5.890 PMID:3379585 [VERIFIED-2]

formal_3: Jones DN & Paulhus DL (2014). Introducing the Short Dark Triad (SD3). Assessment 21(1):28-41. DOI:10.1177/1073191113514105 PMID:24322012 [VERIFIED-2]

OVERLAP with E1-1: L4-L5 here is superiority + entitlement, not worth. SciAm URL resolved (HTTP 200); title taken from slug, not read.

definition: Hypersensitive, insecure self-absorption: entitlement and resentment beneath fragile self-worth.
taxonomy: Hendin & Cheek HSNS · Pincus PNI vulnerability factor
formal_1: Hendin HM & Cheek JM (1997). Assessing hypersensitive narcissism: a reexamination of Murray's Narcism Scale. J Res Pers 31(4):588-599. DOI:10.1006/jrpe.1997.2204 [VERIFIED-1]

Hendin & Cheek DOI via Crossref; the plugin returned nothing.

definition: Shallow affect and lack of remorse or concern for others' suffering (primary psychopathy).

taxonomy: Levenson LSRP primary · Lilienfeld PPI coldheartedness · Patrick triarchic meanness

definition: Enjoyment of others' pain or humiliation, including vicariously, in ordinary life.

definition: Refusal to cheat, steal or corrupt even when it would pay and go unseen.
taxonomy: HEXACO H2 Fairness · Schmitt Justice Sensitivity Inventory
formal_1: Ashton MC & Lee K (2007). Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure. Pers Soc Psychol Rev 11(2):150-166. DOI:10.1177/1088868306294907 PMID:18453460 [VERIFIED-2]

Flair is the nearest verified PT page (no PT "greed" page exists — 404 checked); also Ashton & Lee (2007) [VERIFIED-2] as taxonomy.

definition: Generalized expectancy that outcomes follow one's own actions (internal) versus luck, fate or powerful others (external).
neighbors: Self-Efficacy · Hope (col A) · Anxiety (inverse, col A)
taxonomy: Rotter I-E Scale (1966) · Levenson IPC
formal_1: Rotter JB (1966). Generalized expectancies for internal versus external control of reinforcement. Psychol Monogr 80(1):1-28. DOI:10.1037/h0092976 PMID:5340840 [VERIFIED-2]

L6 (over-internal: blames self for the uncontrollable) is JUDGED; Rotter's scale tops out at L5. Shares the Judge et al. (2002) [VERIFIED-2] core with E1-1 and E1-2.

definition: Extent to which one reads the social situation and tailors one's self-presentation to it.
taxonomy: Snyder Self-Monitoring Scale (1974; 18-item 1986)
formal_1: Snyder M (1974). Self-monitoring of expressive behavior. J Pers Soc Psychol 30(4):526-537. DOI:10.1037/h0037039 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Gangestad SW & Snyder M (2000). Self-monitoring: appraisal and reappraisal. Psychol Bull 126(4):530-555. DOI:10.1037/0033-2909.126.4.530 PMID:10900995 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Day DV, Schleicher DJ, Unckless AL & Hiller NJ (2002). Self-monitoring personality at work: a meta-analytic investigation of construct validity. J Appl Psychol 87(2):390-401. DOI:10.1037/0021-9010.87.2.390 PMID:12002965 [VERIFIED-2]
flair_1: Mark Snyder — Public Appearances, Private Realities: The Psychology of Self-Monitoring (W.H. Freeman, 1987) [UNVERIFIED]
notes: Contested: Gangestad & Snyder argue it is unitary and near-categorical; Lennox & Wolfe (1984, not cited) split it. Also Snyder M & Gangestad S (1986) J Pers Soc Psychol 51(1):125-139 DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.51.1.125 [VERIFIED-1] for the 18-item revision. Neither pole is the "bad" one — L1 is a virtue for authenticity, L5 for diplomacy; only L6 is JUDGED over-shoot. Second flair not found; blank.

definition: Habitual way of managing feeling: rethinking the situation (reappraisal) versus hiding the feeling (suppression).
neighbors: Trait Mindfulness · Moodiness (col A) · Expressiveness (col A)
taxonomy: Gross & John Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ, 2003)
formal_1: Gross JJ & John OP (2003). Individual differences in two emotion regulation processes: implications for affect, relationships, and well-being. J Pers Soc Psychol 85(2):348-362. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.85.2.348 PMID:12916575 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Aldao A, Nolen-Hoeksema S & Schweizer S (2010). Emotion-regulation strategies across psychopathology: a meta-analytic review. Clin Psychol Rev 30(2):217-237. DOI:10.1016/j.cpr.2009.11.004 PMID:20015584 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Webb TL, Miles E & Sheeran P (2012). Dealing with feeling: a meta-analysis of the effectiveness of strategies derived from the process model of emotion regulation. Psychol Bull 138(4):775-808. DOI:10.1037/a0027600 PMID:22582737 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: The ERQ has two independent subscales; the L-row collapses them into one suppression→reappraisal axis BY DESIGN (a persona die needs one row) — say so if the assembler wants two. Gross JJ (1998) Rev Gen Psychol 2(3):271-299 DOI:10.1037/1089-2680.2.3.271 [VERIFIED-1] is the process-model root. Webb et al. note expressive suppression is not useless — L1/L2 are costly, not incompetent.

definition: Dispositional tendency to attend to present experience with open, non-judging awareness.
neighbors: Emotion Regulation Style · Self-Compassion · Boredom Proneness (inverse, col A)
taxonomy: Brown & Ryan MAAS · Baer FFMQ
formal_1: Brown KW & Ryan RM (2003). The benefits of being present: mindfulness and its role in psychological well-being. J Pers Soc Psychol 84(4):822-848. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.84.4.822 PMID:12703651 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Baer RA, Smith GT, Hopkins J, Krietemeyer J & Toney L (2006). Using self-report assessment methods to explore facets of mindfulness. Assessment 13(1):27-45. DOI:10.1177/1073191105283504 PMID:16443717 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Baer RA, Smith GT, Lykins E, Button D, Krietemeyer J, Sauer S, Walsh E, Duggan D & Williams JMG (2008). Construct validity of the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire in meditating and nonmeditating samples. Assessment 15(3):329-342. DOI:10.1177/1073191107313003 [VERIFIED-1]
notes: MAAS is single-factor attention/awareness; FFMQ has five facets (observe, describe, act with awareness, non-judge, non-react) — the L-row scales the general factor. Baer 2008 authors, volume and pages confirmed from the Crossref record (PubMed plugin not run for it). L6 (detachment) is JUDGED, not a scale pole.

definition: Chronic orientation toward gains and aspirations (promotion) versus safety and duties (prevention).
neighbors: Self-Efficacy · Optimism (col A) · Anxiety (col A, prevention side)
taxonomy: Higgins Regulatory Focus Questionnaire (2001) · Lockwood GRFM
formal_1: Higgins ET (1997). Beyond pleasure and pain. Am Psychol 52(12):1280-1300. DOI:10.1037/0003-066X.52.12.1280 PMID:9414606 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Lanaj K, Chang CH & Johnson RE (2012). Regulatory focus and work-related outcomes: a review and meta-analysis. Psychol Bull 138(5):998-1034. DOI:10.1037/a0027723 PMID:22468880 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Higgins ET, Friedman RS, Harlow RE, Idson LC, Ayduk ON & Taylor A (2001). Achievement orientations from subjective histories of success: promotion pride versus prevention pride. Eur J Soc Psychol 31(1):3-23. DOI:10.1002/ejsp.27 [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Heidi Grant Halvorson & E. Tory Higgins — Focus: Use Different Ways of Seeing the World for Success and Influence (Hudson Street Press, 2013) [UNVERIFIED]
notes: Promotion and prevention are two scales, not one (RFQ); the L-row puts prevention low and promotion high BY DESIGN — a person can be high on both, which the row cannot show. Also Lockwood P, Jordan CH & Kunda Z (2002) J Pers Soc Psychol 83(4):854-864 DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.83.4.854 PMID:12374440 [VERIFIED-2] for the GRFM. Lanaj: prevention links to conscientiousness/avoid temperament, promotion to openness/approach.

definition: Readiness to feel self-conscious moral emotion after wrongdoing, and whether it lands on the act (guilt) or the self (shame).
taxonomy: Tangney TOSCA · Cohen GASP
formal_1: Tangney JP, Wagner P & Gramzow R (1992). Proneness to shame, proneness to guilt, and psychopathology. J Abnorm Psychol 101(3):469-478. DOI:10.1037/0021-843X.101.3.469 PMID:1500604 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Cohen TR, Wolf ST, Panter AT & Insko CA (2011). Introducing the GASP scale: a new measure of guilt and shame proneness. J Pers Soc Psychol 100(5):947-966. DOI:10.1037/a0022641 PMID:21517196 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Tangney JP, Stuewig J & Mashek DJ (2007). Moral emotions and moral behavior. Annu Rev Psychol 58:345-372. DOI:10.1146/annurev.psych.56.091103.070145 PMID:16953797 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Shame- and guilt-proneness are separate TOSCA/GASP scales; the row orders them by adaptiveness (Tangney: guilt repairs, shame withdraws/attacks) — L3-L4 is the guilt band, L5-L6 the shame band, L1-L2 absence of both. This is a JUDGED ordering for a persona die, not the instruments' geometry. Also Tangney JP & Dearing RL (2002) Shame and Guilt, Guilford [VERIFIED-1]; Tangney et al. (1996) J Pers Soc Psychol 70(4):797-809 DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.70.4.797 PMID:8636899 [VERIFIED-2]. Marcus 2014 links spite to "guilt-free shame" — neighbour to E2-6.
